raw_case_text:
A 34-year-old male patient presented with high-grade continuous fever associated with chills and rigor for 7 days, persistent severe headache for 6 days, multiple episodes of vomiting, and disorientation for 5 days. There was a history of multiple episodes of GTCS for last 4 days. He had also purpuric spots in lower extremities for last 4 days.
On neurological examination, she had neck rigidity with positive Kernig sign. GCS Score was E1M4V2. No cranial nerve abnormality was noted. Motor examination revealed hypotonia on all four limbs. Planter was bilateral extensor. Rest of the CNS examination could not be done. Other systems were also within normal limit.
MRI scan of brain (plain and contrast), done on 8th day of fever, showed mild diffusion restricted altered signal intensity (hypointense in T1, hyperintense in T2, and FLAIR) in both thalamic and splenium of corpus callosum region [Figure 6], and the diagnosis of dengue meningoencephalitis was done.
Again, treatment was started only with IV fluid, paracetamol as antipyretic and anticonvulsant. Patient had several episodes of GTCS till 7th day of hospital admission. Then it gradually decreased and 12th day onward he had no episode of GTCS. Neck rigidity was absent on 16th day. Thereafter he had an uneventful hospital stay and was discharged on 21st day.
He was the only patient to have IgM dengue positivity in CSF.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 34-year-old male presenting with a 7-day history of continuous high-grade fever with chills and rigors, headache, vomiting, disorientation, lower extremity purpura, and recurrent seizures.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Continuous high-grade fever with chills and rigors began 7 days prior. Severe headache developed 6 days prior, followed by recurrent vomiting and disorientation for 5 days. For the 4 days prior to admission, he experienced multiple generalized tonic-clonic convulsions and noted purpuric spots on his lower extremities.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, chills, rigors, headache, vomiting, disorientation, convulsions, and purpura. Medications and allergies: null.

objective.physical_examination: Comatose/stuporous, GCS score E1M4V2 (7/15). Skin: Purpuric lesions on bilateral lower extremities. Neurological: Nuchal rigidity present with positive Kernig's sign; no cranial nerve palsies; generalized hypotonia across all four limbs; bilateral extensor plantar responses. Other systemic examinations normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Lumbar puncture / CSF analysis: Positive for dengue-specific IgM antibodies by MAC-ELISA. Brain MRI (plain and contrast) on day 8 of fever: Mild diffusion-restricted altered signal intensity (hypointense on T1, hyperintense on T2 and FLAIR) in both thalami and the splenium of the corpus callosum.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Severe neurodengue / acute dengue meningoencephalitis with bilateral thalamic and corpus callosum splenium involvement and lower extremity purpura. Diagnostic confirmation: Positive dengue virus IgM in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) by MAC-ELISA and characteristic neuroimaging findings.
Plan & Outcome: Treated with intravenous fluids, paracetamol, and anticonvulsant therapy. Generalized tonic-clonic seizures recurred until hospital day 7, after which seizure frequency decreased, with complete cessation from day 12 onward. Nuchal rigidity resolved by day 16, sensorium cleared, and the patient was discharged after 21 days with full recovery.
